note: Rules of the multi-problem composition engine (p2-content-extensions-s02, DT-220). Source: Medical Walkthrough v5.1 section 14B.5 (recipe for building any new combination, 8 steps) and the problem-type table beside it. The engine composes the STRUCTURE of a new multi-problem case from problems of approved cases; it writes no clinical value. Everything it outputs is a synthetic DRAFT fixture for practice-pool planning: not clinically validated, not a case file.
ladder_note: Order of the problem-type table (recipe step 2 and 3). A new combination is ordered by it; ties keep the source rank.
max_problems_note: No authored case has more than 4 problems (corpus count: 15 with one, 16 with two, 16 with three, 6 with four).
end_state_order_note: Least to most diversion from the planned pathway; the source end states of content/end_states.csv. 'failure' is never an expected end state of a correct path.
s1_optimisable_note: Recipe step 5: S1 proceeds only if NO optimisable or blocking problem remains; with an optimisable problem in the combination the correct path ends postponed.
cross_checks_note: Recipe step 4 and table 14B.3: every planned drug, fluid and scan is checked against these seven; the engine lists which are touched by the chosen problems and leaves the checking of values to authoring.
requires_sex_note: A problem about pregnancy needs a female patient (the same fact blocks.py uses for female-only history). No other sex or age requirement is invented.
contradiction_note: Recipe step 4 in structural form: one problem's action says to avoid or not do a thing that another problem's action tells the trainee to do. Detected on the plain action text, so it can only miss, never invent, a conflict; a missed conflict is caught by Stage B and review.
